brief: Morgan Stanley's 2027 outlook argues the AI capex cycle remains intact, keeping macro and earnings growth resilient, and that this, combined with cheapened valuations after 2026's de-rating, justifies moving to max overweight global equities, funded from fixed income, commodities and cash, while pairing that risk-on stance with a quality bias given unusually long bull-bear tails. Post-midterm Democrat state wins in Texas and Ohio raise data center political risk, but existing approvals are argued to insulate most 2027 projects, so capex forecasts stay unchanged with only a partial shift of US projects from 2028 into 2029. On financing, the capex mix shifts toward shorter-life IT hardware, which the bank argues drives record AI-related debt issuance and a credit bifurcation: high-quality hyperscalers retain broad access to capital while lower-rated hyperscalers and neoclouds rely more on secured and structured financing. The Fed, ECB and BoJ are each expected to hike twice more over the next 12 months, yet Morgan Stanley expects yields to land below market-implied forward pricing. In FX, a 'Carry Regime' is argued to support a modest further dollar rally even as the euro and yen underperform.
